name: Isolated Retinal Racemose Hemangioma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Imaging Criteria for Retinal Racemose Hemangioma

criteria.description: Presence of dilated, tortuous retinal arteriovenous communications without an intervening capillary bed on fundoscopic examination
Fluorescein angiography demonstrating early filling of dilated veins and absence of capillary phase
No evidence of intracranial or systemic arteriovenous malformations on neuroimaging and systemic evaluation
Presence of visual disturbances such as decreased visual acuity or visual field defects

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria must be met: characteristic fundoscopic appearance, confirmatory fluorescein angiography findings, and absence of systemic arteriovenous malformations.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of Wyburn-Mason syndrome and other systemic AV malformations.

searchTerms: enlarged twisted blood vessels in retina

pathognomonic.symptomName: Early venous filling on fluorescein angiography
searchTerms: early vein filling in eye imaging
fast venous blood flow on eye scan

imaging: Fundoscopic examination revealing dilated tortuous retinal vessels
Fluorescein angiography showing early venous filling and absence of capillary phase
MRI/MRA brain and orbit to exclude intracranial AV malformations
other: Absence of systemic arteriovenous malformations distinguishes isolated form from Wyburn-Mason syndrome

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of intracranial and systemic arteriovenous malformations
Neurological symptoms such as seizures or hemiparesis
Presence of capillary hemangiomas with feeder vessels
Different angiographic pattern with capillary proliferation

references: Gass JD. Stereoscopic Atlas of Macular Diseases. 4th ed. 1997.
Shields JA, Shields CL. Vascular tumors of the retina and choroid. Int Ophthalmol Clin. 2003;43(1):41-64.
